lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | Aug 2022 - Jul 2024
- Owned the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards across two major releases and the on-call rotation that used them.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases, adding automated regression checks that shortened release cycles from 2 weeks to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: Make sure this links directly to the relevant code, GitHub, technical portfolio, or project page rather than a generic landing page.
items.because: The header currently gives no indication that the link contains substantial technical work.

items.says: Add a concise professional positioning line beneath your contact information, tailored to the role you want.
items.because: The resume currently makes the reader infer whether you are targeting ML engineering, LLM/agent infrastructure, robotics software, or general backend engineering.

items.says: Add the expected graduation status only if it is relevant to your target roles, and consider adding selected coursework or research only if it strengthens the chosen target.
items.because: The degree is current and relevant, but the resume does not explain what technical direction the degree supports.

items.says: Make the concurrent student/intern arrangement obvious through consistent location, enrollment, or internship formatting if needed.
items.because: The overlap is plausible, but a reader may briefly wonder whether the dates are incorrect.

items.says: Consider removing the location if space is needed and use the space for relevant academic distinction, coursework, research, or honors.
items.because: The degree title and institution are more important than the location.

items.says: Add a measurable operational outcome and clarify the scope of 'owned.'
items.because: 'Owned' signals responsibility, but the bullet currently proves only that you maintained dashboards and participated in on-call.

items.says: Clarify the operational relationship between the dashboards and the on-call rotation.
items.because: 'The on-call rotation that used them' is awkward conceptually.

items.says: Verify and clarify whether the measurements came from production, staging, or load tests; the request volume or test conditions; whether the 200 ms threshold was a service-level objective or engineering threshold; cache invalidation/freshness constraints; and the scope of the improvement.
items.because: The only missing information is scope and measurement context.

items.says: Specify what the regression checks tested and distinguish your direct contribution from general pipeline maintenance.
items.because: 'Automated regression checks' is broad and the outcome is compelling but unclear.

items.says: Split this into separate accomplishments or substantially reduce the number of claims in one bullet. Clarify which result came from which action.
items.because: The bullet currently combines multiple actions and results, creating causal ambiguity.

items.says: Verify that 'removed' is literally accurate; use a more precise level of improvement if the backlog was reduced rather than eliminated.
items.because: It is not clear whether the backlog was eliminated or just reduced.

items.says: Consider moving this section before the robotics role if your target is LLMs, agent systems, or applied ML.
items.because: The most recent completed role should generally receive the strongest visual priority.

items.says: Clarify your ownership and define the backlog metric.
items.because: 'Triage branch' is company-specific language and the 68% result is strong but undefined.

items.says: Correct the interpretation of the result and define the evaluation setup.
items.because: The bullet needs a clear definition of the metric and experimental setup.

items.says: Do not describe an 8-point increase as a 12% increase unless you explicitly mean relative improvement.
items.because: The distinction between percentage points and relative improvement should remain consistent.

items.says: Add the baseline and clarify the apparent tension between 'single-request' inference and 'dynamic batching.'
items.because: Dynamic batching usually groups multiple requests, while 'single-request edge inference' may imply one request at a time.

items.says: Add hardware or edge environment, throughput impact, and accuracy impact if quantization required validation.
items.because: Needs enough context to be credible to an inference-engineering reviewer.

items.says: Fix the sentence structure and clarify what specifically produced the improvement.
items.because: It is a grammatical fragment and lists several mechanisms without establishing causality.

items.says: Explain whether the 5% reduction was statistically or operationally meaningful and what the baseline comparison was.
items.because: The effect may be small relative to other results and needs context.

items.says: Add evidence that this change improved training in a meaningful way.
items.because: As written, this describes an implementation choice but not its value.

items.says: Add evidence of adoption or operational effect.
items.because: The impact is not yet measurable.

items.says: Replace this bullet with a concrete technical or adoption result from the project.
items.because: It contains broad claims but no defined practice, measurable outcome, scope, or evidence of adoption.

items.says: A reduction from 900 ms to 600 ms is approximately 33%, not 50%.
items.because: The arithmetic error is a serious credibility problem.

items.says: Clarify whether the 900 ms and 600 ms values are measured under the same workload, and whether cache hits, tool-call volume, or accuracy changed.
items.because: The underlying result is strong, but context is missing.

items.says: Describe this as a 12-percentage-point increase unless you also provide the relative improvement, which is approximately 17%.
items.because: The current phrase is ambiguous between percentage points and relative improvement.

items.says: Clarify number of benchmark tasks, whether the benchmark was deterministic or repeated, and whether retries increased latency, tool calls, or cost.
items.because: The tradeoff matters to a hiring manager.

items.says: Add your role in designing, implementing, validating, or maintaining the metrics.
items.because: The bullet should make your contribution and the adoption significance unmistakable.

items.says: Clarify whether you were the primary contributor or one of several contributors, and the project's user or contributor scale if meaningful.
Explain what was degraded, what the evaluator score represented, and why Kendall correlation was the appropriate measure.
items.because: Without experimental context it can look like a disconnected number.

items.says: Clarify whether 0.89 is Kendall’s tau, whether the correlation was statistically significant, and whether the trials were independent.
Quantify or specify the consequence of the defects and clarify what 'fixed upstream' means.
items.because: The impact is currently implicit.

items.says: Explain whether the defects affected benchmark validity, reproducibility, or production behavior.
Move Git into a tools/version-control category or omit it if space is limited.
items.because: Git is expected and is not a differentiating skill.

items.says: Reorganize the skills into technically meaningful groups and ensure every emphasized skill is supported by the resume.
items.because: A skills section should reinforce evidence, not introduce unsupported keywords.

items.says: Either add supporting experience for Kubernetes or remove it.
items.because: Kubernetes currently appears only in skills and nowhere in the accomplishments.

items.says: Choose the target role first, then prioritize the resume accordingly.
items.because: The document does not yet tell the reader which one is the central direction.
